text:
maya: seeing a sudden uptick in Pending GPU pods in us-west-2 after the consolidation test this morning. ~120 pods stuck, most with reason: "ContainerCreating" due to IP allocation failures. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/infra/gpu-provisioning

devon: link? running into ENI limits again? which provisioner handled the scale event?

maya: it's the gpu-provisioner-usw2 (Karpenter). here's the root snippet i grabbed from the provisioner: ```apiVersion: karpenter.sh/v1alpha5
kind: Provisioner
metadata:
  name: gpu-provisioner-usw2
spec:
  requirements:
    - key: kubernetes.io/arch
      operator: In
      values: [amd64]
  provider:
    instanceTypes: [p4dn.xlarge] # we tested consolidation to prefer smaller gpus
    subnetSelector: {aws-usage: private}
  consolidation: {enabled: true}
  limits:
    resources:
      cpu: null
      nvidia.com/gpu: 200
```

chloe: ah, we pinned instanceTypes to a single family for cost testing — if ENI per-instance is low it can saturate IPs quickly. might need to broaden instanceTypes to include g5/g5a/gn5.

liam: also saw drift in node labels after the AMI bake last week — some nodes lost the 'eni-trunking: true' label which reduces ENI capacity assumptions in our scheduler calculations. could be contributing.

sam: short-term mitigation: disable consolidation on that provisioner and allow bursting to larger instances with more ENIs. long-term: warm pool or keep a small reserved capacity.

infra-bot: [alert] GPU pending pods > 100 in cluster=prod-usw2 (2026-03-18T12:12:14Z). Suggested runbook: "increase instanceTypes, disable consolidation, verify ENI quotas".

maya: plan of attack i propose: 1) add 2 more instance families to provisioner (g5.x, g5a.x), 2) flip consolidation=false for 30m, 3) create temporary NodePool with 10 warm GPU nodes in different subnets, 4) monitor. i can push the change for #1 and #2 as a canary.

devon: good. paste the kube patch you'll use here before applying. also run `kubectl get pods -o wide | grep Pending | wc -l` and share output so SRE board can track.

maya: kube command output now: 118

maya: patch i'll apply: ```kubectl patch provisioner gpu-provisioner-usw2 --type merge -p '{"spec": {"provider": {"instanceTypes": ["p4dn.xlarge","g5.xlarge","g5a.xlarge"]}, "consolidation": {"enabled": false}}}'```

chloe: +1. after that we should also add a tolerance for ip exhaustion at scheduler level: add a podTopologySpread or nodeAffinity for multi-az spread so ENI hotspots don't hit one subnet.

liam: i'll audit the AMI label drift — if nodes are dropping eni-trunking label on rotation, open issue with AMI bake job. assigning to me.

sam: i'll draft short playbook for this pattern (ENI exhaustion during consolidation) and recommend default provisioner settings for GPU pools. we should include cost delta for moving to larger instances vs warm pool.

maya: applying patch in ~2m. will post status. :rocket:

infra-bot: kube-event: Deployment/gpu-workloads in default namespace recorded NodeAffinityFailed for 23 pods.

maya: patch applied. new events showing scale-up to g5.xlarge types. pending count dropping to 42.

devon: excellent. leave consolidation off for 1h and re-evaluate. also check any IAM rate limits for ENI creation across AZs.

chloe: note for follow-up: run a capacity model that includes ENI per-instance + ENI trunking multiplier; we underestimated effective IPs per GPU node when mixing instance families.

liam: opened GH issue: "AMI bake removes eni-trunking label intermittently" (#3421).

sam: created ops card: "ENI exhaustion -> provisioner fallback playbook" and linked to incident doc.

maya: current pending 9, most scheduling now. will monitor for 30m then re-enable consolidation if stable. thanks all. :thumbsup:

devon: bring back consolidation only after we validate warm-pool and instance family mix. otherwise we flip flop costs.

chloe: also add a canary that simulates IP pressure (small job that spawns hostNetwork pods) so we don't regress.

maya: noted. final note: we should track per-node ENI utilization in the console to alert earlier next time. filing follow-up ticket.
